description: A driving and route-learning simulator built from real places.
headline:
Linux runs reviewed.
Follow-ups tracked.
summary: The Chrome frame stall and recorded memory growth are deferred for later investigation. Next: plan selection and continuity.

integration.title: Integration is a separate step
integration.note: Reviewed driving and Linux qualification remain on their branch. Canonical main holds the generation foundation.

next.label: Next conversation
next.title: Plan selection & continuity
next.note: The stall and memory issues are tracked for later. Neither blocks this planning discussion.

stages.title: Project setup
stages.summary: An application shell with a working 3D viewport and clear module boundaries.
stages.outcome: A stable starting point for the simulator.

stages.title: Zone compiler
stages.summary: One immutable OpenStreetMap snapshot becomes deterministic roads, buildings and a street graph.
stages.outcome: Validated geometry, provenance and reproducible artifacts.

stages.title: Zone generation
stages.summary: Coordinate-based generation qualified across five real cells, extended with place search and local on-demand builds.
stages.outcome: Choose a place, build its zone, recover from errors and reuse the verified result.

stages.title: Driveability
stages.summary: Drive, collide, inspect and recover inside one flat cell. Linux Chrome/Firefox evidence is independently reviewed; the remaining stall and memory investigations are tracked for later.
stages.outcome: Reliable desktop driving, supported by explicit qualification evidence.

phases.title: Physical world
phases.detail: Ground, building collision, clearance and a marked play boundary.

phases.title: First vehicle
phases.detail: Safe spawn, real physics, steering, braking, reverse and recovery.

phases.title: Driving interaction
phases.detail: Keyboard/touch controls, chase camera, pause and inspection ownership.

phases.title: Qualification
phases.detail: Linux cold/keyboard, all four sustained cases and 20-cycle lifecycle evidence pass review. The Chrome RAF stall and recorded process-memory growth remain unresolved in issues #2 and #1. Mac and iPad checks remain deferred.

phases.title: Desktop benchmark
phases.detail: A fixed Chicago control tape, deterministic checkpoints and bounded Chrome trace capture.

stages.title: Selection & continuity
stages.summary: Define richer map selection and cache behavior, then how adjacent cells connect during driving.
stages.outcome: Move between selected areas with understandable loading and continuity.

stages.title: Geographic fidelity
stages.summary: Add the slopes, crossings and geographic details that materially improve recognition and orientation.
stages.outcome: Places become recognizable enough to support spatial memory.

stages.title: Training experience
stages.summary: Build a complete route-learning session with progressive aids, recovery from mistakes and a useful review.
stages.outcome: Practice a route, understand difficult decisions and repeat with fewer aids.

gates.title: #2 · Chrome frame stall
gates.detail: Deferred for investigation and fix. Independent RAF stopped while timers continued; later passing runs have not established a cause or fix.

gates.title: #1 · Memory growth & GC
gates.detail: Deferred for investigation. Complete Linux process/GPU observations are retained; passing Chrome JS limits does not certify a resident-memory plateau.

decisions.title: Chrome stall tracked
decisions.detail: The user deferred the unexplained frame stall alongside recorded memory growth. Preserve the incomplete attempt and require evidence of a fix or validated mitigation before closing the issue. It does not block next-stage planning.

decisions.title: Memory & GC follow-up
decisions.detail: Investigate resident process-memory growth, allocation pressure and garbage collection later. The issue now includes complete Chrome/Firefox lifecycle observations and their limits. No new profiling campaign is active.

decisions.title: Linux Chrome + Firefox now
decisions.summary: Safari removed; Mac and iPad deferred.
decisions.detail: The user removed Safari from desktop scope and deferred macOS Edge testing. This continuation covers Linux Chrome/Firefox only; deferred platforms are not passed.

decisions.title: Linux memory method agreed
decisions.detail: Use unchanged post-GC JS limits where available, stable ownership counts, browser-tree PSS for resident native/WASM mappings and separate GPU allocations. Do not sum them or invent a new threshold after measurement.

decisions.title: Plan the next boundary
decisions.detail: Stage 04 planning can proceed with both issues explicitly deferred. This scheduling decision does not claim unconditional Driveability acceptance or authorize later-stage implementation.

decisions.title: Keep the foundation intact
decisions.detail: Preserve schema-v1, provenance, bounded acquisition and the compiler/runtime separation. Hosted generation remains a separate decision.

decisions.title: Keep phases lean
decisions.detail: The roadmap is living. Discuss implementation at the next phase boundary; promote necessary backbone work explicitly and remove duplicated scope.

milestones.title: A reproducible world
milestones.text: Immutable OSM, roads, buildings and a street graph.

milestones.title: Build somewhere new
milestones.text: Place search, local generation and connection recovery.

milestones.title: A vehicle to drive
milestones.text: Real physics, collision, chase view and recovery.

milestones.title: Two Linux engines checked
milestones.text: Five-cell controls, sustained runs and 20-cycle lifecycle records.

evidence.title: Current follow-up decision
evidence.note: 9 September: unresolved stall and memory work deferred to issues #2 and #1; next-stage planning can continue.

evidence.title: Champion independent review
evidence.note: Independent full verification, raw-evidence checks, memory assessment and remaining acceptance concerns.

evidence.title: Roadmap & current direction
evidence.note: Stage ordering and the current platform scope.

evidence.title: Linux qualification evidence

evidence.title: Earlier desktop benchmark
evidence.note: The reviewed Chicago control tape and saved-trace parser foundation.

handoffs.detail: Tracked in issue #1 alongside next-phase planning.

handoffs.detail: Implementation reviewed; full stage acceptance remains open.
